subject: Maths
chapter: Introduction to Trigonometry and Its Applications

questions.q: Evaluate tan1° x tan2° x tan3° x ... x tan89°.
questions.explanation: Pair tan1° with tan89°, tan2° with tan88°, and so on. Since tan(90°-theta) = cot(theta), every paired product equals tan(theta)cot(theta) = 1. The remaining middle factor is tan45° = 1, so the whole product is 1.

questions.q: For an acute angle A, sin A = 1/2. What is cot A?
questions.explanation: For an acute angle, sin A = 1/2 corresponds to A = 30°. At 30°, cos A = sqrt(3)/2. Therefore cot A = cos A / sin A = sqrt(3).

From 4tan(theta) = 3, we have 4sin(theta)/cos(theta) = 3, so 4sin(theta) = 3cos(theta). The numerator becomes 3cos(theta) - cos(theta) = 2cos(theta). The denominator becomes 3cos(theta) + cos(theta) = 4cos(theta), so the ratio is 1/2.

questions.q: If sin(theta) - cos(theta) = 0 for an acute angle, what is sin^4(theta) + cos^4(theta)?
questions.explanation: The condition gives sin(theta) = cos(theta). Together with sin^2(theta) + cos^2(theta) = 1, this means each square equals 1/2. Therefore sin^4(theta) + cos^4(theta) = 1/4 + 1/4 = 1/2.
